decisions.note: The print shows the waqf sign ۖ above the end of ٱلْأَرْضِ. The project encodes waqf signs as a separate token after a space, as Tanzil does and as every earlier final batch does (quran.py merges it with the word). B's attached form would raise a false Quran flag.

At 600 dpi the closing ornament ﴾ after فَحَدِّثْ touches the reference parenthesis «(الضحى: ١١)» with no space, although the justified line widens every other space. Both keyers wrote it glued. The verse words match Tanzil exactly. The flag is only a tokenization artefact of the glued reference, not a Quran variant, so A is kept as printed.

print_errors.note: Printed with dotless final ى (the body font draws its automatic small alif over it), where the word is the interrogative أي; kept as printed.
The parenthetical opened by the dash at the end of p.031 («فقال لي الشيخ الحسيني –») has no closing dash on p.032; nothing added.

keyA.notes: All four pages continue the previous page (029+ because p.028 ends «صعب علي العلم،»; 030+, 031+ and 032+ continue mid-sentence). No footnotes, headings or glosses in this batch. Prose dashes on p.030 («أقول – تقريرًا») and at the end of p.031 are written as the printed en dash U+2013 with spaces. In p.030 the reference «(الضحى: ١١)» is printed touching the closing ornament with no space, so it is written glued: «فَحَدِّثْ﴾(الضحى: ١١)». quran.py reports one quran_extra_word flag for this token only because of that gluing; the verse text matches Tanzil. The second reference «(يوسف: ٥٥)» is printed with a space after ﴾. Both references use round parentheses, as printed. Waqf sign ۖ on ٱلْأَرْضِ is written as a separate token after a space, as in Tanzil. Dotless final ى in the Quran is kept as printed (ٱجْعَلْنِى، إِنِّى). Honorifics printed as words (رضي الله عنه، رضي الله عنهم، عليه السلام، عليهما السلام، رحمه الله) are kept as ordinary text; the two printed ﷺ glyphs (pp.031, 032) are kept as U+FDFA. «شريف منسب» on p.032 is clearly printed منسب and is transcribed as is. «حديثيا» on p.031 has no tanween in the print.

print_errors.note: printed with dotless ى (font adds its small alif) where وأي is expected; kept as printed
hamza on waw as printed (expected رُئيت); kept as printed
printed منسب (م ن س ب) clearly; possibly intended منتسب/النسب; kept as printed

keyB.notes: All four pages continue the previous page's sentence, so every marker has '+'; p028 has no footnotes, and pp.029-032 have no footnotes. On p030 the closing bracket of the Duha quotation touches the reference parenthesis in print, so it is written ﴾(الضحى: ١١) with no space; the Yusuf reference has a printed space: ﴾ (يوسف: ٥٥). In the Yusuf 55 quotation the print has dotless final ى in ٱجْعَلْنِى and إِنِّى (Madinah style), the hamza+kasra drawn under the tooth in خَزَآئِنِ (encoded ئِ as in Tanzil, madda as ا+U+0653), and the ۖ waqf sign over ٱلْأَرْضِ (attached to the word). The dashes after «أقول» (p030) and «الحسيني» (p031) are written as en dash –. Honorifics رضي الله عنه/عنهم, عليه السلام, رحمه الله are printed as ordinary words (no glyphs); ﷺ glyph on pp.031 and 032 kept.
